support-zoe: Hey team, incoming from ACME — they've been getting 503s to the hosted inference API since ~2024-06-04 12:14 UTC. They reported timeouts and traces show upstream worker failures. Can we triage?

oncall-bot: [ALERT] incident detected: hosted-api-503-spike (severity: high). Alert @sre-aaron @infra-devin @eng-emma

sre-aaron: I'm looking. Customer logs show spike in 503s at 12:13:55 -> 12:15:10 UTC. Initial hypothesis: upstream worker abort during hot request fanout under high qps.

support-zoe: Link to customer trace: https://console.redwood/acme/traces/abcd1234 — request ids: r-7f3, r-7f4. They sent long prompts (18k tokens) and concurrent requests ~120.

infra-devin: pulling relevant pod logs now. Running: `kubectl -n hosted logs infer-worker-5f7b --since=30m`

infra-devin: quick log snippet: ```
[12:14:03] runtime.cc:482] Exception: segfault (signal 11) in infer_runner
[12:14:03] gpu_memory.cc:301] GPU allocation failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[12:14:03] backtrace: 0x7f9c... kernel/attn.cu:line 123
```

sre-aaron: OOM + segfault combo. Looks similar to earlier prefetched-kv memory regressions but different stack. Any recent batchmap/dynbatch changes?

eng-emma: We did a dynbatch tweak in canary yesterday (reduce max batch consolidation threshold). But that should reduce OOM risk, not increase. Also rolled a tiny kernel optimization to attn path last night. I'll check the diff.

eng-emma: Repro attempt on staging with same model + long context + QPS=100: I see worker memory climb, then occasional `std::bad_alloc` followed by SIGSEGV. Repro steps: `ab -n 500 -c 120 -p longprompt.json http://staging-hosted/api/v1/generate`

support-zoe: Customer is asking for mitigation — can we enable fallback routing to smaller model / disable the new canary? They need immediate relief.

sre-aaron: For mitigation I suggest 1) enable fallback routing (route to model-x-small) for ACME tenant, 2) temporarily pin request concurrency per-worker to 32 for hosted pool, 3) roll back the attn kernel change on canary. I'll run (1) and (2) now.

infra-devin: Done: fallback routing enabled for tenant/acme -> model-x-small. Also applied per-worker max-concurrency=32 via config service. Monitoring.

oncall-bot: [ACTION] routing-change applied by infra-devin at 12:22:01 UTC.

support-zoe: ACME confirms errors dropped and tail latency improved after the fallback. They still want root cause and plan to avoid in future.

eng-emma: I'm bisecting the attn kernel change. Likely culprit: an index calculation on long sequences that can underflow on edge lengths, triggering illegal memory access when combined with certain dynbatch patterns. Reproduced with a crafted test. Will open PR to revert and add regression test.

sre-aaron: Good. Next steps: (A) eng revert + regression test, (B) increase worker OOM logging and heap dump on segfault for faster triage, (C) run targeted soak tests at QPS=150 with 16k+ contexts. I'll own (B) and (C).

infra-devin: For immediate postmortem, capturing coredump from `/var/crash/infer_runner.*` and collecting nvml logs. I've archived `/var/log/infer_worker/` from affected hosts.

support-zoe: I'll send ACME a summary and ETA for fix. Thanks team — marking as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:

eng-emma: PR opened: #4827 revert/attn-fix + unit test for long-context indexing. ETA for deploy to canary: 2 hours once reviewed.

sre-aaron: I'll follow up with a short postmortem including timeline and runbook changes (limit long-request concurrency by default, improve autoscale heuristics for OOM avoidance).

support-zoe: Noted. If anything changes ping me. Closing customer escalation when PR deploys and we verify no recurrence in canary.

infra-devin: final note: found one host with older nvidia-driver mismatch that may worsen memory fragmentation — patching images tonight.

sre-aaron: Thanks. Closing thread for now.
